SDD as a team-level discipline for Agentic Software Engineering with a 'methodological harness' of eight mechanisms (authors' framework), no version, no tool. Tools mentioned as examples only: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex (technical harness), OpenSpec-style proposal-apply-archive cycle

System specifications (architecture, conventions, domain models, normative rules) materialised as always-loaded rule files (agent.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, AGENTS.md); feature specifications per change (intent, acceptance criteria in Given-When-Then, constraints, decisions), archived when delivered; skills (SKILL.md, loaded on demand); persistent shared knowledge store (decisions, rationale, session summaries); consultation records; evidence packs (acceptance tests mapped to clauses, CI output, rationale, links to spec and rules); workflow definitions with autonomy levels

Iterative cycle over specifications: proposal (lightweight spec enriched iteratively) -> apply (agent derives artefacts, suspends to consult on ambiguity) -> archive (verified spec committed; later changes reference it). Harness mechanisms: H1 context engineering, H2 persistent shared knowledge, H3 executable specifications, H4 N-version parallel agents (git worktrees), H5 normative specifications, H6 structured consultation, H7 evidence-backed acceptance, H8 graduated autonomy

Briefing (human writes/approves spec, with review of briefs); structured consultation when agent suspends on ambiguity; review of evidence packs against the spec before acceptance; norm encoding via reviewed PR; autonomy calibrated per task class (e.g. auth changes need human-approved plan and step-wise review; dependency patches fully autonomous)
